title.ko: 확신의 정도를 가르는 조동사: might well · can't possibly · is bound to · ought to be
title.en: degrees of certainty: might well, can't possibly, is bound to, ought to be

explain.ko: 확신의 정도는 조동사로 세밀하게 나타냅니다. must / be bound to는 거의 확실한 추론, ought to / should는 기대에 비춘 추론, might well은 충분히 있을 법한 가능성을 나타냅니다. can't possibly는 강한 부정 추론입니다. 과거에 대한 추론은 조동사 + have + 과거분사를 씁니다. 또한 likely, probable, undoubtedly 같은 어휘로 확신을 더 정교하게 조절할 수 있습니다.
explain.en: Degrees of certainty are expressed finely with modals. Must and be bound to signal near-certain deduction, ought to and should signal expectation-based deduction, and might well signals a quite likely possibility. Can't possibly is a strong negative deduction. For the past, use modal + have + past participle. Words such as likely, probable and undoubtedly adjust certainty further.

notes.ko: might well은 might보다 가능성이 한층 높게 들립니다.
notes.en: Might well sounds more probable than plain might.

notes.ko: 과거 추론에는 반드시 have + 과거분사를 쓰세요.
notes.en: Past deduction requires have + past participle.

notes.ko: 근거가 약하면 단정을 피하고 신중한 표현을 선택하세요.
notes.en: With weak evidence, avoid asserting and choose a cautious form.

lines.t: Distinguishing degrees of certainty is central to precise English. Use must or be bound to when you are sure, might well when you leave a possibility open, and can't possibly when you rule something out. If the evidence is weak, avoid asserting and express yourself cautiously.

trans.ko: 확신의 정도를 구별하는 것은 정확한 영어의 핵심입니다. 확실할 때는 must나 be bound to를, 가능성을 열어 둘 때는 might well을, 불가능하다고 볼 때는 can't possibly를 씁니다. 근거가 약하다면 단정하지 말고 신중하게 표현하세요.

prompt.ko: 확신의 정도를 달리하는 조동사를 사용해 어떤 사건의 원인에 대한 추론을 4문장으로 써 보세요.
prompt.en: Write four sentences reasoning about the cause of an event, using modals of different degrees of certainty.

task.model: The server stopped suddenly. The update might well be the cause. But the developers can't possibly have skipped the tests. Once we check the logs, the cause is bound to emerge. Whoever is in charge ought to know by now.

model_trans.en: The server stopped suddenly. The update might well be the cause. But the developers can't possibly have skipped the tests. Once we check the logs, the cause is bound to emerge. Whoever is in charge ought to know by now.
